title: Unsafe Mutex Poison Propagation
pattern: Invoking a panic or abort statement while actively holding a mutable reference or lock on shared state (e.g., inside a lock guard scope).
why_bad: State safety violation. Panicking while holding a Mutex poisons the lock. Any other thread that subsequently attempts to acquire the Mutex will get a `PoisonError` and crash, spreading a single thread's failure like a contagion across the system. [15, Chapter 11, "panic setting"]
detection: A `panic!`, `unwrap()`, or `expect()` within the scope of an acquired mutex/rwlock guard.
counterexample: Highly critical security kernels where lock poisoning is explicitly desired to freeze all threads upon any suspected memory corruption.
source: *Jon Gjengset - Rust for Rustaceans*, Chapter 11 / Chapter 10, "panic settings" [15]
